about: Evidence recommendations for the UAE Information Assurance Standard v2.1 library (uae_ia.json). Authored for this library: the standard itself names no evidence. Every item is grounded in the control's own statement, sub-controls or implementation guidance, and 'covers' lists the numbered sub-controls (1), 2) ...) it helps to evidence; every sub-control of every control is covered by at least one item. build_uae_ia_catalog.py merges this file into the generated catalog as evidence_requirements {name, description, filetype} and drops 'covers'; collection_frequency is kept where the control is event-driven or continuous (the seeder reads it from dict entries and otherwise defaults to annually).

M1.1.1.name: Interested parties register
M1.1.1.description: Register of the internal and external parties relevant to the entity's information security, with the owner of each relationship.

M1.1.1.name: Requirements of interested parties

M1.1.1.name: External context analysis
M1.1.1.description: Analysis of the sector, national, legal, regulatory and threat-environment factors that affect the entity's information security program.

M1.1.1.name: Internal capabilities assessment
M1.1.1.description: Assessment of the people, funding, skills and systems available to the information security program.

M1.1.1.name: Organization chart
M1.1.1.description: Current chart of the entity's organizational structure showing where information security sits and who holds each role.

M1.1.2.name: Top management approval of security direction
M1.1.2.description: Signed approval or minutes showing top management established the information security policy and objectives and aligned them with the entity's strategic direction.

M1.1.2.name: Security requirements built into business processes
M1.1.2.description: Extracts from business process documents showing where information security requirements are integrated into the entity's activities.

M1.1.2.name: Resource commitment approvals
M1.1.2.description: Budget, headcount and tooling approvals showing top management made the resources the information security program needs available.

M1.1.2.name: Top management communications on information security
M1.1.2.description: Messages or briefings from top management on why effective information security management matters and on conforming to the standard's requirements.

M1.1.2.name: Top management review of information security
M1.1.2.description: Minutes of top management reviews of information security risks, controls and effectiveness, showing the direction given, the decisions taken and whether the intended outcomes are being achieved.

M1.1.2.name: Continual improvement and management support record
M1.1.2.description: Record of improvement actions promoted by top management and of the support it gave other management roles to demonstrate leadership in their own areas.

M1.1.3.name: Assignment of responsibility and authority
M1.1.3.description: Top management's documented assignment of the responsibility and authority for conformity with the standard and for presenting information security performance to top management.

M1.1.3.name: Information security performance report
M1.1.3.description: Report from the assigned role to top management on how information security is performing against the standard.

M1.1.3.name: Appointment of the information security lead
M1.1.3.description: Appointment letter or role description naming the management or leadership team member with overall responsibility for information security and the dedicated function that supports them.

M1.1.3.name: Information Security Committee charter
M1.1.3.description: Terms of reference establishing the Committee to oversee and govern information security, with its membership, mandate and cross-functional role.

M1.1.3.name: Information Security Committee minutes
M1.1.3.description: Minutes showing the Committee meets, oversees information security and drives its integration across functions and departments.

M1.2.1.name: Approved information security policy
M1.2.1.description: Documented policy appropriate to the entity's purpose that frames the setting of information security objectives and commits to satisfying applicable requirements, including legal and regulatory ones, and to continual improvement.

M1.2.1.name: Top management approval of the policy
M1.2.1.description: Signed approval page, resolution or minutes showing top management established and approved the current version.

M1.2.1.name: Policy review and revision record
M1.2.1.description: Version history and review records showing the policy is maintained, reviewed and updated at planned intervals and when significant changes occur.

M1.2.1.name: Policy communication to staff
M1.2.1.description: Evidence the policy was communicated within the organization, such as staff notices or briefing records.

M1.2.1.name: Policy availability to interested parties
M1.2.1.description: Evidence of where and how the policy is made available to relevant interested parties, such as a screenshot of the publication location or a distribution list.

M1.2.2.name: Documented information security objectives
M1.2.2.description: Objectives set at relevant functions and levels, consistent with the information security policy and measurable where practicable.

M1.2.2.name: Objectives basis record
M1.2.2.description: Working showing the objectives take account of the entity's context and mission, applicable requirements, risk assessment results and risk treatment results.

M1.2.2.name: Approval of the objectives
M1.2.2.description: Sign-off or minutes showing management approved the current objectives.

M1.2.2.name: Objectives communication record
M1.2.2.description: Evidence the objectives were communicated within the entity, such as notices or briefings.

M1.2.2.name: Objectives update record
M1.2.2.description: Records of reviews showing the objectives were updated as appropriate, with version history.

M1.2.3.name: Approved supporting policy set
M1.2.3.description: The set of topic-specific information security policies, each approved and showing its owner, intended audience and version.

M1.2.3.name: Policy coverage matrix
M1.2.3.description: Matrix mapping every aspect of the standard that applies to the entity after the risk assessment, and every national, Emirate and sector requirement, to the policy that addresses it.

M1.2.3.name: Policy-to-practice consistency review
M1.2.3.description: Review confirming each policy reflects what the entity has actually implemented and contains no statement the entity does not comply with.

M1.2.3.name: Policy publication and communication record
M1.2.3.description: Evidence the supporting policies were published and communicated to employees and relevant external parties.

M1.2.3.name: Personnel acknowledgement records
M1.2.3.description: Records of relevant personnel acknowledging the supporting policies that apply to them.

M1.2.3.name: Supporting policy review log
M1.2.3.description: Log of reviews at planned intervals and after significant changes, with the updates that resulted.

M1.3.1.name: Information security budget and staffing plan
M1.3.1.description: Budget and staffing plan showing the human and financial resources allocated to the information security program and why they are adequate for the work.

M1.3.1.name: Competence requirements for security roles
M1.3.1.description: Defined competence, in terms of education, training or experience, needed by the people doing work that affects information security performance.

M1.3.1.name: Staff competence records
M1.3.1.description: Records of qualifications, training history and experience showing the people in information security roles are competent.

M1.3.1.name: Competence gap actions and effectiveness evaluation
M1.3.1.description: Actions taken to acquire missing competence, such as training or hiring, and the evaluation of whether each action worked.

M1.3.2.name: Communication plan
M1.3.2.description: Documented plan stating what is communicated, when, with whom, by whom and how, for internal and external information security communication.

M1.3.2.name: Authority and lead entity contact list
M1.3.2.description: Current contact details and channels for the relevant authorities, including the UAE lead entities for cyber security.

M1.3.2.name: Correspondence with authorities
M1.3.2.description: Sample correspondence exchanged with authorities or lead entities showing adequate communication is maintained.

M1.3.3.name: Document control procedure
M1.3.3.description: Procedure covering approval before issue, review and update, revision identification, legibility, storage, availability, distribution, disposal, external-origin documents, obsolete versions and retained documents.

M1.3.3.name: Controlled document register
M1.3.3.description: Register of controlled documents showing owner, version, approval date, classification, review date, whether the document is of external origin and its retention identification.

M1.3.3.name: Document approval records
M1.3.3.description: Sample of approval records showing documents were approved before issue.

M1.3.3.name: Repository access and distribution settings
M1.3.3.description: Screenshots of the document repository permissions and distribution lists showing documents are available to those who need them, stored by classification and distributed under control.

M1.3.3.name: Document disposal records
M1.3.3.description: Records showing documents were disposed of according to their classification, and obsolete versions were withdrawn.

M1.3.3.name: Mandatory controls compliance record
M1.3.3.description: Document recording the entity's compliance with each mandatory control of the standard, with a reference to the supporting evidence.

M1.3.4.name: Project management procedure with security requirements
M1.3.4.description: Project management procedure showing information security risk assessment and requirement identification built into the project life cycle.

M1.3.4.name: Project information security risk assessments
M1.3.4.description: Sample project risk assessments and treatment plans showing information security risks assessed at an early stage and again through the project life cycle.

M1.3.4.name: Project security requirements
M1.3.4.description: Sample project requirement and specification documents listing the information security requirements identified early and how they were implemented.

M1.3.4.name: Risk treatment progress and effectiveness review
M1.3.4.description: Project or steering committee reviews of risk treatment progress, with the results of tests that evaluate whether the treatment is effective.

M1.3.5.name: Special interest groups register
M1.3.5.description: List of the relevant national and international interest groups, working groups, security forums and professional associations, with the entity's membership status and contact.

M1.3.5.name: Rules on what participants may share
M1.3.5.description: Guidance defining what employees participating in interest groups are allowed to share.

M1.3.5.name: Circulated interest group information
M1.3.5.description: Examples of advisories or updates from interest groups circulated inside the entity, as the groups' rules permit.

M2.1.1.name: Approved risk management policy
M2.1.1.description: Documented policy, approved by management, that addresses the purpose and scope for critical services and their supporting functions and defines the roles and responsibilities of the risk management team.

M2.1.1.name: Risk criteria definitions
M2.1.1.description: Defined risk acceptance, likelihood, impact and risk evaluation criteria, with the scales and thresholds used to apply them.

M2.1.1.name: Risk treatment and monitoring strategy
M2.1.1.description: The strategy for treating risks and the strategy for monitoring and reviewing them, as set out by the entity.

M2.1.1.name: Risk assessment approach
M2.1.1.description: Criteria and steps for performing, reviewing and updating risk assessments, with the guidance that keeps repeated assessments objective, consistent, valid and comparable.

M2.1.1.name: Risk assessment consistency check
M2.1.1.description: Comparison of repeated assessments, or of the same risks assessed by different people, showing the results are consistent and comparable.

M2.1.1.name: Risk management policy approval and version history
M2.1.1.description: Approval record and version history of the risk management policy, with evidence it is applied in the entity's risk assessments.

M2.2.1.name: Risk identification results
M2.2.1.description: Documented results of the risk identification, listing the risks to the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the entity's information.

M2.2.1.name: Risk owner assignments
M2.2.1.description: Record naming the owner of each identified risk.

M2.2.1.name: Level of detail decision
M2.2.1.description: Documented decision, with the reasons, on the level of detail and the approach used for the information security risk assessment.

M2.2.2.name: Consequence assessment
M2.2.2.description: Assessment of the consequences of a loss of confidentiality, integrity or availability for each identified risk, based on the business importance of the asset.

M2.2.2.name: Likelihood assessment
M2.2.2.description: Assessment of the realistic likelihood of each risk occurring, based on the existing controls and the identified vulnerabilities and threats.

M2.2.2.name: Threat and vulnerability inputs
M2.2.2.description: Threat information and vulnerability findings used to judge the likelihood of each risk.

M2.2.2.name: Risk analysis results
M2.2.2.description: Documented analysis showing the level determined for each risk and the consequence and likelihood ratings behind it.

M2.2.3.name: Risk evaluation results
M2.2.3.description: Documented comparison of each analyzed risk with the risk criteria the entity has established, showing which risks are acceptable and which need treatment.

M2.2.3.name: Treatment priorities
M2.2.3.description: Prioritized list of the risks to be treated, with the reasons for any priority given beyond the risk level.

M2.2.3.name: Evaluation results shared with lead entities
M2.2.3.description: Evidence the risk evaluation results were shared with the UAE lead entities for cyber security where required, such as the transmittal message and any reply.

M2.3.1.name: Treatment option decisions
M2.3.1.description: Record of the option selected for each assessed risk (modification, retention, avoidance or sharing) and the reasons for the choice.

M2.3.1.name: Risk acceptance approvals
M2.3.1.description: Formal approvals from risk owners, passed to top management, for risks retained under the risk acceptance criteria.

M2.3.1.name: Residual risk and treatment effectiveness review
M2.3.1.description: Review of whether residual risk levels are tolerable, the new treatment generated where they are not, and how effective each treatment is.

M2.3.2.name: Control selection record
M2.3.2.description: Record of the controls selected for each risk treatment decision, starting from the controls in the standard and showing the risk each control addresses.

M2.3.2.name: Control omission check
M2.3.2.description: Check that every applicable control of the standard was considered during control selection, with the gaps found and how they were closed.

M2.3.2.name: Entity-specific additional controls
M2.3.2.description: List of controls identified in addition to those in the standard, with the risk or requirement that calls for each.

M2.3.2.name: Control selection criteria review
M2.3.2.description: Review showing the risk acceptance criteria and the legal, regulatory and contractual requirements taken into account when controls were selected.

M2.3.3.name: Risk treatment plan
M2.3.3.description: Documented plan setting out the management actions, resources required, responsibilities and priorities for managing each information security risk.

M2.3.3.name: Treatment implementation schedule
M2.3.3.description: Schedule giving the target date for implementing each identified control, with its owner and progress.

M2.3.3.name: Treatment plan approval
M2.3.3.description: Sign-off by the accountable approver that the plan, with its resources and responsibilities, is accepted.

M2.3.4.name: Statement of Applicability
M2.3.4.description: Document listing the controls identified as necessary, the reason each was identified and its current implementation status.

M2.3.4.name: Risk-to-control traceability
M2.3.4.description: Mapping from each treated risk to the controls that address it, supporting the reasons given in the Statement of Applicability.

M2.3.4.name: Implementation status evidence
M2.3.4.description: Status report or test results supporting the implementation status recorded for the controls in the Statement of Applicability.

M2.3.4.name: Control exclusion justifications
M2.3.4.description: Justification for each risk-based applicable control of the standard that the entity excludes, with the risk assessment result that supports it.

M2.4.1.name: Risk review and update procedure
M2.4.1.description: Documented procedure for planned and ad hoc review and update of the risk assessment and treatment, with the defined periodicity and the major changes that trigger a review.

M2.4.1.name: Risk factor monitoring records
M2.4.1.description: Records of monitoring of asset values, impacts, threats, vulnerabilities and likelihood that show changes in the entity's context being identified.

M2.4.1.name: Risk review records
M2.4.1.description: Records of the regular review of all risks, including accepted risks, and of the reviews held after major changes.

M2.4.1.name: Risk management improvement record
M2.4.1.description: Record of the monitoring and review of risk management, with the improvements made.

M2.4.2.name: Risk communication plan
M2.4.2.description: Plan for communicating risk information with key stakeholders, including decision-makers, at every stage of risk management.

M2.4.2.name: Risk communication records
M2.4.2.description: Records of risk information shared with stakeholders and of their input, such as briefings, messages and consultation notes.

M2.4.2.name: Decision-maker risk briefings
M2.4.2.description: Briefings or reports to decision-makers on the existence, nature, likelihood, severity, treatment and acceptability of risks.

M3.1.1.name: Approved awareness and training policy
M3.1.1.description: Documented policy, approved by management, that is appropriate to the entity's purpose, facilitates implementation of the associated controls and outlines the roles and responsibilities of providers and recipients.

M3.1.1.name: Awareness and training objectives
M3.1.1.description: Objectives set using the policy's framework, with the factors considered when identifying them.

M3.1.1.name: Provider and recipient role assignments
M3.1.1.description: List of the people or teams who provide awareness and training and the groups who receive it, with their responsibilities.

M3.1.1.name: Awareness and training policy approval and review history
M3.1.1.description: Sign-off and version history showing the awareness and training policy is documented, approved and maintained, with the date of its last review.

M3.2.1.name: Approved awareness and training program
M3.2.1.description: Program, with its approval and version history, covering how people doing work under the entity are informed of its information security requirements, their contribution to its effectiveness and the implications of not conforming.

M3.2.1.name: Awareness delivery records
M3.2.1.description: Attendance or completion records showing people doing work under the entity were informed of its information security requirements, their contribution and the implications of not conforming.

M3.2.1.name: Training and other actions delivered
M3.2.1.description: Records of the training or other actions delivered to meet the needs of personnel whose work affects information security.

M3.2.1.name: Effectiveness evaluation of actions taken
M3.2.1.description: Evaluation of whether the training and other actions taken were effective.

M3.2.1.name: Education, skills and qualification records
M3.2.1.description: Records of the education, training, skills, experience and qualifications of personnel performing work that affects information security.

M3.3.1.name: Required information security skills
M3.3.1.description: List of the information security skills the entity needs.

M3.3.1.name: Current skills assessment
M3.3.1.description: Assessment of the information security skills currently in place in the entity.

M3.3.1.name: Skills gap analysis
M3.3.1.description: Analysis of the gaps between the required and current information security skills, which gives the training needs.

M3.3.2.name: Training solution per need
M3.3.2.description: Record of the training solution identified for each training need, with its medium and target audience.

M3.3.2.name: Training implementation plan
M3.3.2.description: Plan with the timeline for delivering each training solution to its target audience.

M3.3.2.name: Training resource allocation
M3.3.2.description: Budget or resource approvals showing the resources needed to run the training are allocated to the program.

M3.3.3.name: Training delivery records
M3.3.3.description: Attendance and completion records showing training was delivered in line with the implementation plan.

M3.3.3.name: Plan variance and alternative solutions record
M3.3.3.description: Record of problems met against the implementation plan and the alternative training solutions identified in response.

M3.3.3.name: Updated training implementation plan
M3.3.3.description: Current version of the plan, checked against the identified training needs to show all of them are still met.

M3.3.4.name: Before and after knowledge measurements
M3.3.4.description: Results of measuring information security knowledge and skills before and after the training plan, such as test scores.

M3.3.4.name: Training outcome evaluation
M3.3.4.description: Evaluation of whether the training delivered meets the expected outcomes against the entity's knowledge requirements.

M3.3.4.name: Training corrective actions
M3.3.4.description: Record of the actions taken to improve or replace training solutions that did not reach the expected outcome.

M3.3.5.name: Individual training records
M3.3.5.description: Documented training record for each person targeted by information security training, covering basic awareness and specific training.

M3.3.5.name: Training records periodic check
M3.3.5.description: Periodic check showing all stakeholders have completed the necessary training, with follow-up on those who have not.

M3.3.5.name: Training record retention evidence
M3.3.5.description: Evidence that individual training records are kept for the period the entity has set.

M3.4.1.name: Awareness campaign scope
M3.4.1.description: Definition of each campaign's audience, internal and external, and of its content, based on the security risks relevant to users' activities.

M3.4.1.name: Awareness campaign timeline
M3.4.1.description: Timeline for deploying the specific awareness campaigns so that the program objectives are met.

M3.4.1.name: Campaign delivery evidence
M3.4.1.description: Samples of the campaign materials issued, such as emails, posters or session invitations, dated against the timeline.

M3.4.1.name: Campaign adjustment record
M3.4.1.description: Record of problems against the timeline, the alternative campaigns identified and the updated campaign checked against the program objectives.

M3.4.1.name: Awareness campaign records
M3.4.1.description: Comprehensive records of every campaign run: dates, audience reached, content and participation.

M4.1.1.name: Background verification procedure
M4.1.1.description: Procedure defining the checks in line with relevant laws and ethics and proportionate to the business requirements, the classification of the information to be accessed and the perceived risks.

M4.1.1.name: Completed verification check reports
M4.1.1.description: Reports showing verification checks were completed for sampled candidates, contractors and third-party personnel.

M4.1.1.name: Verification coverage review
M4.1.1.description: Review of the current staff, contractors and third-party personnel against their verification records, showing none is missing a check.

M4.1.1.name: Verification document handling
M4.1.1.description: Evidence that background verification documents are held securely, such as the access permissions on their storage and the retention arrangement.

M4.1.2.name: Standard information security terms and conditions
M4.1.2.description: Template terms and conditions stating the information security responsibilities of employees, contractors, third parties and the entity.

M4.1.2.name: Contracts containing information security terms
M4.1.2.description: Sample signed employment, contractor and third-party contracts that include the information security terms and conditions.

M4.1.2.name: Understanding and acceptance records
M4.1.2.description: Signed confirmation that each person has understood and agreed the terms, such as signed terms and confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements.

M4.1.2.name: Contract review and amendment record
M4.1.2.description: Record of the review of existing contracts and of the amendments made to add the information security terms.

M4.2.1.name: Security policy notification records
M4.2.1.description: Evidence that employees, contractors and third parties were informed of the security policies they must comply with, such as notices and distribution lists.

M4.2.1.name: First-access acceptance screen
M4.2.1.description: Screenshot of the first-access screen that presents the relevant security policy or guidelines for the user to read and accept.

M4.2.1.name: User acceptance records
M4.2.1.description: Records of users accepting the security policy at first access, with the date and the version accepted.

M4.2.2.name: Formal disciplinary process
M4.2.2.description: Documented disciplinary process for information security policy violations by employees, contractors and third-party users.

M4.2.2.name: Disciplinary process awareness evidence
M4.2.2.description: Evidence that people in the entity have been made aware of the disciplinary process, such as notices, induction material or briefing records.

M4.2.2.name: Disciplinary action records
M4.2.2.description: Records showing the process was enforced for confirmed breaches, with the verification that a breach occurred and the action taken, identities protected as required.

M4.2.2.name: Security breach register
M4.2.2.description: Register of the information security breaches committed, with the date, the people involved and the outcome.

M4.3.1.name: Termination and change of employment procedure
M4.3.1.description: Procedure defining which information security responsibilities and duties remain valid after termination or change of employment, including confidentiality and intellectual property rights.

M4.3.1.name: Continuing duties in contracts
M4.3.1.description: Sample contracts and confidentiality agreements stating the duties that continue after employment ends and for how long.

M4.3.1.name: Communication of continuing responsibilities
M4.3.1.description: Records that leavers and people changing role were told of their continuing responsibilities, such as exit notices and signed acknowledgements.

M4.3.2.name: Asset return procedure
M4.3.2.description: Termination and change of employment steps for recovering all issued software, documents, equipment and other assets, including how the assets to be returned are identified.

M4.3.2.name: Asset return records
M4.3.2.description: Completed return checklists or signed receipts for the assets recovered from leavers and people changing role.

M4.3.2.name: Leaver asset reconciliation
M4.3.2.description: Reconciliation of the assets issued to sampled leavers against those returned, with follow-up on anything outstanding.

M5.1.1.name: Compliance requirements identification procedure
M5.1.1.description: Procedure, with the assigned responsibility, for identifying on an ongoing basis all statutory, regulatory and contractual compliance requirements that apply to the entity.

M5.1.1.name: Legal, regulatory and contractual requirements register
M5.1.1.description: Register of the applicable legislation and requirements for information security, each with the individual responsible for meeting it and the controls in place.

M5.1.1.name: System requirements from compliance obligations
M5.1.1.description: Record of the specific system requirements that follow from each identified compliance requirement.

M5.1.1.name: Compliance requirement to control mapping
M5.1.1.description: Mapping of each compliance requirement to the specific controls that ensure it is met.

M5.1.1.name: Periodic review of compliance requirements
M5.1.1.description: Records of reviews of the compliance requirements and associated controls for completeness, and of the updates they led to.

M5.1.2.name: Intellectual property rights policy
M5.1.2.description: Documented policy defining the legal use of software and information products, with its version and review history.

M5.1.2.name: Intellectual property requirements identification
M5.1.2.description: Process description and resulting list of the requirements the entity must meet to protect intellectual property rights.

M5.1.2.name: Intellectual property system requirements
M5.1.2.description: Record of the specific system requirements arising from those requirements, such as limits on the number of licensed users.

M5.1.2.name: License and ownership register
M5.1.2.description: Register of licensed products with proof of ownership of licenses, master disks and manuals, and the checks that only authorized and licensed software is installed.

M5.1.2.name: Intellectual property controls review
M5.1.2.description: Periodic review of the intellectual property requirements and associated controls for completeness.

M5.1.3.name: Record identification procedure
M5.1.3.description: Process for identifying records with specific compliance requirements on loss, destruction, falsification, unauthorized access and unauthorized release.

M5.1.3.name: Records inventory and retention schedule
M5.1.3.description: Inventory of record types, such as accounting and database records, each with its retention period, storage medium and protection requirements.

M5.1.3.name: Record protection controls
M5.1.3.description: Evidence of the controls protecting important records, such as access permissions, integrity protection and archive or backup settings.

M5.1.3.name: Record protection requirements review
M5.1.3.description: Periodic review of the record protection requirements and associated controls for completeness.

M5.1.4.name: Data privacy and protection policy
M5.1.4.description: Documented policy covering data handling, security, breach management and the rights of data subjects, with its review history.

M5.1.4.name: Applicable data protection laws register
M5.1.4.description: Register of the data protection and privacy laws, regulations and contractual clauses that apply to the data the entity handles, with the compliance status for each.

M5.1.4.name: Personal data handling inventory
M5.1.4.description: Inventory of the critical business activities that handle PII or SPI, with the owner of each.

M5.1.4.name: Privacy risk assessments
M5.1.4.description: Privacy risk assessments carried out for the critical activities that handle PII or SPI.

M5.1.4.name: Privacy control implementation
M5.1.4.description: Evidence of the security controls implemented to meet the data protection and privacy requirements, each linked to the requirement it meets.

M5.1.4.name: Data breach detection and response procedure
M5.1.4.description: Procedure for detecting, responding to and reporting data breaches, particularly those affecting PII and SPI.
