M5.2.1.name: Compliance check results
M5.2.1.description: Results of the compliance checks carried out, including technical compliance reports where automated tools are used.

M5.2.1.name: Checker and reviewer authorization
M5.2.1.description: Record showing the people who perform and review compliance checks are authorized and have adequate capabilities, such as role assignments and qualifications.

M5.2.1.name: Non-compliance tracking
M5.2.1.description: Register of the non-compliance detected, with the causes, the report to the appropriate authority, the corrective action and its review.

M5.3.1.name: Approved audit access requests
M5.3.1.description: Audit requests for access to systems and data, each with the approval of the appropriate management.

M5.3.1.name: Technical audit test scope agreement
M5.3.1.description: Agreed scope of the technical audit tests, including the systems covered and the level of access granted.

M5.3.1.name: Audit access restrictions and clean-up
M5.3.1.description: Evidence that audit access was limited as agreed, such as read-only accounts and removal of copies of system files after the audit.

M6.1.1.name: Approved performance evaluation policy
M6.1.1.description: Documented policy, approved by management, that sets the overall framework for all performance evaluations in the entity.

M6.1.1.name: Performance results reporting methods
M6.1.1.description: The methods by which performance evaluation results are reported to management, such as report formats, audiences and routes.

M6.1.1.name: Measurement integration model
M6.1.1.description: Description of how detailed control measurements are combined with higher-level measures for information security objectives, risk management and incident management.

M6.1.1.name: Performance evaluation output sample
M6.1.1.description: Sample output produced under the policy showing detailed control measurements integrated with the higher-level measures and reported to management.

M6.2.1.name: Monitoring and measurement plan
M6.2.1.description: Plan stating what is monitored and measured, including information security processes and controls, when and by whom, and when and by whom the results are analyzed and evaluated.

M6.2.1.name: Monitoring and measurement methods
M6.2.1.description: Documented methods for monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation, showing how they ensure valid results.

M6.2.1.name: Monitoring and measurement results
M6.2.1.description: Documented results of monitoring and measurement of information security processes and controls, such as performance indicator values.

M6.2.1.name: Performance and effectiveness evaluation
M6.2.1.description: Evaluation, by the assigned people, of the results against the information security performance and the effectiveness of the program.

M6.2.2.name: Internal audit program
M6.2.2.description: Documented program setting the frequency, methods and responsibilities of internal audits and showing the importance of the processes concerned and previous audit results were considered.

M6.2.2.name: Audit plan, criteria and scope
M6.2.2.description: For each audit, the criteria, scope and plan, including the areas to be audited and the people to be met.

M6.2.2.name: Auditor selection and impartiality record
M6.2.2.description: Record of how the auditors were selected and the confirmation of their objectivity and impartiality.

M6.2.2.name: Internal audit reports
M6.2.2.description: Report of each audit giving the results against the entity's own requirements, the requirements of the standard and any applicable Emirate, sector or national requirements.

M6.2.2.name: Audit results reported to management
M6.2.2.description: Evidence the audit results were reported to relevant management, such as the transmittal, presentation or meeting minutes.

M6.2.3.name: Management review schedule
M6.2.3.description: Schedule of the planned management reviews of the information security program, with the agenda showing the required inputs.

M6.2.3.name: Management review inputs
M6.2.3.description: Pack presented to top management: status of earlier actions, changes in issues and interested parties' needs, performance feedback, risk assessment results and treatment plan status, and opportunities for improvement.

M6.2.3.name: Management review minutes
M6.2.3.description: Documented review results with the decisions on continual improvement opportunities and on any changes needed to the information security program.

M6.2.3.name: Management review action tracker
M6.2.3.description: Tracker of the actions arising from each review and their status, used as the input to the next review.

M6.3.1.name: Nonconformity and corrective action procedure
M6.3.1.description: Procedure for reacting to and correcting nonconformities, determining their causes and reviewing the effectiveness of corrective action.

M6.3.1.name: Nonconformity register
M6.3.1.description: Register of nonconformities with the action taken to control and correct each one.

M6.3.1.name: Root cause analyses
M6.3.1.description: Analyses of sampled nonconformities showing the review, the causes determined and whether similar nonconformities exist or could occur.

M6.3.1.name: Corrective action implementation records
M6.3.1.description: Records of the corrective actions implemented, with owner and completion date.

M6.3.1.name: Corrective action effectiveness reviews
M6.3.1.description: Reviews of whether the corrective actions taken eliminated the causes of the nonconformities.

M6.3.2.name: Improvement plan
M6.3.2.description: Plan of improvements to the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the information security controls in place, with owners and target dates.

M6.3.2.name: Improvement decisions from monitoring and review
M6.3.2.description: Record of improvement decisions taken from monitoring and review results, showing the performance measurement results and incidents that prompted each one.

M6.3.2.name: Improvement implementation evidence
M6.3.2.description: Evidence that selected improvements were carried out, such as completed actions or updated documents.

T1.1.1.name: Approved information asset management policy
T1.1.1.description: Documented policy, approved by management, that is appropriate to the entity's complexity and the information assets it manages and provides the framework for managing them, including the assignment of owners.

T1.1.1.name: Bring-your-own-device arrangements
T1.1.1.description: The framework for managing personal devices used for work, stating which devices are allowed and the conditions and controls that apply.

T1.1.1.name: Asset management policy approval and version record
T1.1.1.description: Approval record naming the approver and date, with the version history of the information asset management policy.

T1.2.1.name: Information asset inventory
T1.2.1.description: Inventory of information assets showing for each its type, location, backup information, related licenses and importance or criticality.

T1.2.1.name: Inventory reconciliation with other inventories
T1.2.1.description: Reconciliation of the information asset inventory with the entity's other inventories, such as enterprise asset management and ERP, with differences resolved.

T1.2.1.name: Asset ownership listing
T1.2.1.description: Listing that names the owner with management responsibility for each identified asset and shows any assets still without one.

T1.2.1.name: Inventory update records
T1.2.1.description: Records of additions, changes and retirements of assets showing the inventory is kept up to date.

T1.2.2.name: Acceptable use rules
T1.2.2.description: Documented and approved rules for the acceptable use of information and associated assets, including personal assets used within the entity's environment.

T1.2.2.name: Acceptable use rules circulation record
T1.2.2.description: Evidence the rules were circulated to employees and third parties.

T1.2.2.name: Signed acceptance of the rules
T1.2.2.description: Records of employees and third parties accepting the acceptable use rules.

T1.2.2.name: Acceptable use compliance checks
T1.2.2.description: Results of checks that the rules are followed, such as monitoring results and the action taken on violations.

T1.3.1.name: Information classification scheme
T1.3.1.description: Approved scheme defining the classification levels, based on information value, legal requirements, sensitivity and criticality to the entity.

T1.3.1.name: Classified information sample
T1.3.1.description: Sample of information assets with their classification levels, showing the scheme is implemented.

T1.3.1.name: Classification scheme communication
T1.3.1.description: Evidence the classification scheme was communicated across the whole entity, such as notices, intranet pages or training material.

T1.3.1.name: Classification review records
T1.3.1.description: Records of reclassification and periodic checks showing classifications are kept up to date as value, sensitivity and criticality change over the life cycle.

T1.3.2.name: Information labeling procedure
T1.3.2.description: Procedure for applying labels that reflect the classification to information and related assets in physical and electronic formats, including where and how labels are attached.

T1.3.2.name: Labeled information samples
T1.3.2.description: Samples of labeled documents, files or media in physical and electronic formats showing labels that match the classification.

T1.3.2.name: Labeling exceptions
T1.3.2.description: Record of the cases where labeling is omitted or not technically possible and how each case is handled.

T1.3.3.name: Information handling procedures
T1.3.3.description: Procedures for processing, storing and communicating information consistent with its classification and label, at each classification level.

T1.3.3.name: Access restrictions by classification
T1.3.3.description: Evidence, such as permission and repository settings, that access to information is restricted according to its classification level.

T1.3.3.name: Authorized recipients record
T1.3.3.description: Formal record of the authorized recipients of classified information and other associated assets.

T1.3.4.name: Information transfer rules
T1.3.4.description: Documented rules and procedures for each type of transfer facility, internal and external, reflecting the information classification and regulatory and business obligations.

T1.3.4.name: Information transfer agreements
T1.3.4.description: Agreements with the parties the entity exchanges information with, covering recipient authentication and protection of the information in transit.

T1.3.4.name: Public platform sharing controls
T1.3.4.description: Evidence of the controls that limit what is shared on social media and other public platforms to authorized information, such as approval workflow or blocking rules.

T1.3.5.name: Data leak prevention configuration
T1.3.5.description: Configuration export of the leak prevention rules that identify classified information and block user actions or network transmissions that would expose it, with the systems, networks and devices covered.

T1.3.5.name: Leakage monitoring and detection records
T1.3.5.description: Extract from the monitoring of channels such as email, file transfers and removable media, showing classified information at risk is monitored and disclosure is detected.

T1.3.5.name: Blocked transmission records
T1.3.5.description: Records of user actions or transmissions that were blocked or quarantined because they would expose classified information, with the follow-up taken.

T1.3.6.name: Information deletion procedure
T1.3.6.description: Procedure for securely deleting information by classification level, naming the deletion methods, such as overwriting or cryptographic erasure, and the point at which information is no longer needed.

T1.3.6.name: Deletion records
T1.3.6.description: Records of deletions carried out, with the date, the information or media concerned and the result, including the proof obtained from any service supplier that deleted data for the entity.

T1.3.6.name: Third-party deletion requirements
T1.3.6.description: Clauses in agreements with third parties that store the entity's information requiring its deletion during and when the service ends.

T1.3.6.name: Deletion process review
T1.3.6.description: Periodic review of the deletion process against business requirements, laws and regulations, with the changes made as a result.

T1.4.1.name: Removable media management procedure
T1.4.1.description: Procedure covering the whole life cycle of removable storage media: setup, distribution, use and disposal.

T1.4.1.name: Removable media protection levels
T1.4.1.description: Definition of the protection required for removable storage media at each classification level.

T1.4.1.name: Removable media register
T1.4.1.description: Register of issued removable media with owner, classification and status.

T1.4.1.name: Removable media restriction settings
T1.4.1.description: Configuration or screenshots showing removable media ports and drives are disabled on systems that do not need them, and that auto-run is prevented.

T1.4.1.name: Removable media usage monitoring
T1.4.1.description: Log extract or report of removable media use, with the action taken on unauthorized use.

T1.4.2.name: Media reuse and disposal procedure
T1.4.2.description: Procedure for secure reuse and disposal of media containing classified information, proportionate to the sensitivity of that information.

T1.4.2.name: Media sanitization and destruction records
T1.4.2.description: Records showing media were securely erased or physically destroyed, for example by shredding or incineration, before reuse or disposal.

T1.4.2.name: Media disposal log
T1.4.2.description: Log of disposed storage media with the date, media identifier, disposal method and the person who authorized it.

T1.5.1.name: Endpoint device security requirements
T1.5.1.description: Documented secure configuration and handling requirements for user endpoint devices: information classification they may handle, registration, software restrictions, updates and network connection rules.

T1.5.1.name: Endpoint compliance report
T1.5.1.description: Report from the endpoint management system showing the security measures applied across user endpoint devices, such as encryption, updates, software restrictions and personal firewall.

T1.5.1.name: Automatic lockout configuration
T1.5.1.description: Configuration export or screenshot showing the lockout time applied to unattended user endpoint devices.

T1.5.1.name: Mobile device management enrollment
T1.5.1.description: List of personal devices used for work that are enrolled in mobile device management, with the settings enforced: encryption, passcode and remote wipe.

T1.5.1.name: Work data separation settings
T1.5.1.description: Configuration showing work data is separated from personal data on personal devices through containerization or an equivalent method.

T1.5.1.name: Endpoint logging and monitoring settings
T1.5.1.description: Evidence that logging and monitoring are enabled on user endpoint devices, such as agent status and a sample of the events collected.

T2.1.1.name: Approved physical and environmental security policy
T2.1.1.description: Documented policy, approved by management, that outlines the roles and responsibilities for physical and environmental security and takes account of asset classification and physical location (storage, processing and transfer).

T2.1.1.name: Physical and environmental security procedures
T2.1.1.description: Procedures that implement the policy and its associated physical and environmental protection controls.

T2.1.1.name: Physical security policy approval and review history
T2.1.1.description: Approval and review history of the physical and environmental security policy, with the date it was last reviewed and updated.

T2.2.1.name: Security area classification
T2.2.1.description: Register of the entity's security areas, classified by the assets and information each one holds or handles.

T2.2.1.name: Security perimeter definitions
T2.2.1.description: Site or floor plans showing the perimeter defined for each security level.

T2.2.1.name: Perimeter risk assessment
T2.2.1.description: Risk assessment that sets the siting and strength of each perimeter according to the assets inside it.

T2.2.1.name: Perimeter protection inspection records
T2.2.1.description: Inspection records or photographs showing the walls, doors, locks and alarms that protect each area containing information and information systems.

T2.2.2.name: Secure area entry authentication settings
T2.2.2.description: Access control system configuration or screenshots showing persons are authenticated at the entrances of secure areas, for example by card plus PIN.

T2.2.2.name: Secure area access records
T2.2.2.description: Records of access to secure areas, including the date and time of entry and departure of visitors and the purpose of the visit.

T2.2.2.name: Visible identification requirement
T2.2.2.description: Rule and sample evidence that everyone within the premises wears visible identification, such as the badge types issued and the results of spot checks.

T2.2.2.name: Physical access log review
T2.2.2.description: Access logs from the entry system with evidence that they are updated and monitored, such as review sign-offs and action on anomalies.

T2.2.2.name: Contractor and third-party escort records
T2.2.2.description: Escort procedure and records showing contractors and third parties are accompanied, with the areas explicitly designated for them without escort.

T2.2.2.name: Delivery and loading area access control
T2.2.2.description: Procedure and evidence, such as door controls and receiving records, that access to delivery and loading and unloading areas is controlled.

T2.2.3.name: Public access restriction rules
T2.2.3.description: Rules that prevent access by the public to key facilities, in line with the physical and environmental security policy.

T2.2.3.name: Facility signage review
T2.2.3.description: Inspection records or photographs showing there are no obvious signs, outside or inside, that identify the type of information or activities in secure areas.

T2.2.3.name: Offices and facilities inspection records
T2.2.3.description: Inspection records for offices, rooms and facilities confirming the public access rules are applied and nothing identifies their purpose.

T2.2.4.name: Physical site risk assessments
T2.2.4.description: Risk assessments of each physical site covering natural disasters, malicious attack and accidents, performed before critical operations begin and at regular intervals.

T2.2.4.name: Physical protection countermeasures
T2.2.4.description: Record of the countermeasures and procedures chosen from the assessments, such as fire, flood and explosion protection, with their implementation status.

T2.2.4.name: Physical and environmental threat monitoring record
T2.2.4.description: Record showing changes in the threats to each site, including those from neighboring premises, are monitored and the safeguards adjusted.

T2.2.5.name: Secure area working guidelines
T2.2.5.description: Guidelines for working in secure areas, including need-to-know awareness, avoiding unsupervised work and posted emergency procedures.

T2.2.5.name: Secure area supervision records
T2.2.5.description: Records showing activities in secure areas are supervised, including work by third parties, and that vacant secure areas are locked and checked.

T2.2.5.name: Recording equipment and device authorization
T2.2.5.description: Rules and approvals for the devices allowed into secure areas, including recording equipment and mobile device cameras.

T2.2.5.name: Surveillance coverage and test records
T2.2.5.description: Evidence that secure areas are monitored by surveillance systems, such as the camera and intruder alarm layout and the results of periodic tests.

T2.3.1.name: Equipment siting and protection guidelines
T2.3.1.description: Guidelines for siting and protecting equipment against unauthorized access and damage, such as positioning to limit unnecessary access and viewing of screens by unauthorized persons.

T2.3.1.name: Equipment location inspection records
T2.3.1.description: Inspection records of sampled equipment locations showing the guidelines are applied.

T2.3.1.name: Environmental monitoring configuration
T2.3.1.description: Configuration of the environmental sensors, such as temperature, humidity, water and smoke, with their alert thresholds and recipients.

T2.3.1.name: Environmental alert records
T2.3.1.description: Records of alerts raised for potential environmental threats and the response to each.

T2.3.2.name: Power protection description
T2.3.2.description: Description of the power protection and uninterrupted supply serving information systems, with its capacity and the equipment it covers.

T2.3.2.name: Supporting utilities inspection and test records
T2.3.2.description: Records of regular inspection and testing of power and other supporting utilities showing they function properly.

T2.3.2.name: Emergency lighting test records
T2.3.2.description: Test records showing emergency lighting operates when the main power fails.

T2.3.3.name: Cable tamper protection evidence
T2.3.3.description: Photographs or inspection records showing power and telecommunication cabling is protected against physical tampering, for example by conduits, locked rooms or boxes and controlled access to patch panels.

T2.3.3.name: Cable segregation layout
T2.3.3.description: Cabling layout or inspection record showing power cables are separated from communications cables to prevent interference.

T2.3.3.name: Cable labeling and inspection records
T2.3.3.description: Records of cable labeling at both ends and of physical inspections for unauthorized devices attached to cables.

T2.3.4.name: Supplier maintenance recommendations
T2.3.4.description: Suppliers' recommended service intervals and specifications for the equipment, with evidence they are available to maintenance personnel.

T2.3.4.name: Equipment commissioning and decommissioning procedure
T2.3.4.description: Procedure for commissioning and decommissioning equipment that protects classified data.

T2.3.4.name: Equipment maintenance log
T2.3.4.description: Log of preventive and corrective maintenance and of suspected or actual faults for all equipment, with the personnel who carried out each task.

T2.3.4.name: Maintenance personnel authorization and data clearing
T2.3.4.description: Records showing only authorized personnel serviced equipment and that classified information was cleared, or the personnel were cleared, when equipment left for maintenance.

T2.3.5.name: Off-site equipment protection rules
T2.3.5.description: Rules for protecting equipment used outside the premises, such as not leaving it unattended in public places, observing manufacturers' instructions and preventing viewing of screens in public.

T2.3.5.name: Off-site equipment authorization and custody records
T2.3.5.description: Management authorization and removal records for equipment and media used outside the premises, owned by the entity or privately, with a chain-of-custody log of transfers.

T2.3.5.name: Off-premise location risk assessment
T2.3.5.description: Risk assessment of off-premise locations, such as home-working and temporary sites, with the controls applied as a result.

T2.3.6.name: Equipment disposal and re-use procedure
T2.3.6.description: Procedure for secure disposal or re-use of equipment based on the sensitivity of the stored information, including checking whether storage media is present.

T2.3.6.name: Data removal and destruction evidence
T2.3.6.description: Evidence that classified data and licensed software were removed or securely overwritten, or the media destroyed, before disposal or re-use.

T2.3.6.name: Disposed equipment register
T2.3.6.description: Record of disposed equipment with its identifier, the date, the method and the person responsible.

T2.3.7.name: Clear desk and clear screen policy
T2.3.7.description: Formal policy for papers, removable storage media and screens that is appropriate to the entity's purpose and outlines the responsibilities of users.

T2.3.7.name: Policy availability to users
T2.3.7.description: Evidence the policy is readily available to all users, such as an intranet publication or induction material.

T2.3.7.name: Screen lock configuration
T2.3.7.description: Configuration showing unattended screens lock automatically and need authentication to unlock.

T2.3.7.name: Clear desk inspection results
T2.3.7.description: Results of clear desk and clear screen inspections, with the action taken on findings.

T3.1.1.name: Minimum security configuration standards
T3.1.1.description: Documented minimum security configurations for each common product in use, covering hardware, software, cloud services and network devices, based on vendor or independent security guidance.

T3.1.1.name: Applied configuration evidence
T3.1.1.description: Configuration exports from sampled systems showing the minimum security configurations are implemented.

T3.1.1.name: Configuration compliance monitoring report
T3.1.1.description: Report from the configuration monitoring tool comparing systems with the minimum security configurations and listing the deviations found.

T3.1.1.name: Security configuration review records
T3.1.1.description: Records of periodic reviews of the security configurations and the updates made as a result.

T3.1.2.name: Approved operating procedures
T3.1.2.description: Documented and approved operating procedures giving the detailed instructions for each job, such as system owners, secure installation and configuration, information handling, and backup and resilience, in a format that can be shared with stakeholders.

T3.1.2.name: Operating procedure review records
T3.1.2.description: Review log showing the operating procedures are reviewed periodically and updated.

T3.1.2.name: Operating procedure access and awareness
T3.1.2.description: Evidence stakeholders can access the operating procedures and know about them, such as repository permissions and distribution notices.

T3.1.3.name: Change management procedure
T3.1.3.description: Documented change management procedure covering documentation, specification, testing, approval and managed implementation of changes to information systems.

T3.1.3.name: Change management scope
T3.1.3.description: List of the systems to which the change management process applies.

T3.1.3.name: Change log
T3.1.3.description: Log of all proposed changes with their security impact and the management approval given.

T3.1.3.name: Rollback and communication plans
T3.1.3.description: Rollback, fallback and recovery procedures and communication plans for sampled approved changes.

T3.1.4.name: Environment separation description
T3.1.4.description: Description of the separation between development, test and operational environments, showing the level chosen and the controls that enforce it.

T3.1.4.name: Environment separation settings
T3.1.4.description: Network, domain and access control settings showing the environments run on separate systems or domains and development tools are not reachable from operational systems.

T3.1.4.name: Environment transfer rules
T3.1.4.description: Rules for access to each environment and for moving information, software and systems between them, built into the system and software development life cycle.

T3.1.4.name: Software promotion records
T3.1.4.description: Sample records of software moved from development through test to operational status, showing the transfer rules were followed.

T3.1.5.name: Capacity measurements
T3.1.5.description: Measurements of the current capacity of systems, such as storage, compute and bandwidth use, over time.

T3.1.5.name: Capacity requirements forecast
T3.1.5.description: Estimate of the capacity needed by planned systems and projected growth, taking account of new business and system requirements.

T3.1.5.name: Capacity adjustment and stress test records
T3.1.5.description: Records of the adjustments made to keep system performance at the required level, and of stress tests confirming capacity meets peak demand.

T3.1.6.name: Anti-malware coverage report
T3.1.6.description: Report from the anti-malware console listing the servers, workstations, laptops and other connected devices that are protected and any that are not.

T3.1.6.name: Anti-malware update status
T3.1.6.description: Evidence that the anti-malware tools, their scanning engines and detection definitions are up to date on all protected devices.

T3.1.6.name: Malware scanning configuration
T3.1.6.description: Settings showing system files and files downloaded from public networks are scanned periodically, email attachments are scanned before reaching the inbox and removable media is scanned each time it is connected.

T3.1.6.name: Auto-run disabled configuration
T3.1.6.description: Configuration of servers, workstations and laptops showing content on removable media is not run automatically.

T3.1.6.name: Malware detection events and notifications
T3.1.6.description: Log extract of malware detection events from the anti-malware tools, with the notifications sent to administrators.

T3.1.6.name: Malware awareness records
T3.1.6.description: Awareness material and attendance records covering malware risks, behaviors and preventative actions for users.

T3.1.7.name: Backup requirements
T3.1.7.description: Record of the information and software that needs backup, how often, and the protection required for the backup copies.

T3.1.7.name: Backup procedures
T3.1.7.description: Documented backup procedures and system capabilities for each backup requirement, with the restoration procedures.

T3.1.7.name: Backup job records
T3.1.7.description: Backup job reports showing backups run to schedule and complete, forming an accurate record of the copies made.

T3.1.7.name: Backup restoration test results
T3.1.7.description: Results of routine tests showing backed up information and software can be restored reliably.

T3.1.8.name: Software installation restrictions
T3.1.8.description: Settings and the list of authorized administrators showing unauthorized software is prohibited and only authorized administrators can install software on operational systems.

T3.1.8.name: Software original copy repository
T3.1.8.description: Listing showing an original copy of every installed software, including previous versions, is kept.

T3.1.8.name: Unauthorized software review records
T3.1.8.description: Records of regular reviews to detect unauthorized software or amendments, with the corrective action started.

T3.1.8.name: Software installation audit log
T3.1.8.description: Audit log extract of all software installations on operational systems.

T3.2.1.name: Approved monitoring policy and procedures
T3.2.1.description: Documented policy and procedures outlining what system aspects are monitored, how and how often, and who is responsible for the monitoring activities.

T3.2.1.name: Monitoring to incident response procedure
T3.2.1.description: Procedure defining how information from monitoring activities is taken into the incident response process.

T3.2.1.name: Logging requirements
T3.2.1.description: Defined logging requirements and activities, including the events to capture, the frequency of log reviews and the retention of logs.

T3.2.1.name: Clock synchronization requirements
T3.2.1.description: Defined clock synchronization requirements and related activities.

T3.2.1.name: External information sharing requirements
T3.2.1.description: Record of the Emirate, sector or national requirements on information to be shared with external entities and how the monitoring procedures account for them.

T3.2.1.name: Monitoring policy approval and review record
T3.2.1.description: Approval record and review history of the monitoring policy and procedures, showing they are kept up to date.

T3.2.2.name: Auditable events list
T3.2.2.description: List of the activities captured in audit logs for hardware devices, operating systems and installed applications, with the minimum information recorded for each.

T3.2.2.name: Audit log samples
T3.2.2.description: Log extracts from sampled systems showing the required details are recorded, such as user ID, date and time, event details, device identity and network address.

T3.2.2.name: Log review schedule and records
T3.2.2.description: Defined minimum review frequency for each log source and the records of the reviews carried out.

T3.2.2.name: Log reviewer training and skills
T3.2.2.description: Training and skills records of the personnel who review logs.

T3.2.2.name: Log retention requirements and settings
T3.2.2.description: Defined minimum retention times for all logs and the settings that enforce them.

T3.2.2.name: Critical log protection
T3.2.2.description: Identification of the critical log information across systems and the access, integrity and storage protections applied in proportion to its sensitivity.

T3.2.3.name: Monitored system usage list
T3.2.3.description: List of the types of system usage that are monitored and the minimum information gathered for each monitoring activity.

T3.2.3.name: Monitoring review frequency and records
T3.2.3.description: Defined minimum frequency for reviewing the information gathered and the records of the reviews carried out.

T3.2.3.name: Monitoring reviewer qualifications
T3.2.3.description: Qualification and training records of the personnel who review the information gathered from monitoring.

T3.2.3.name: Monitoring information retention settings
T3.2.3.description: Defined minimum time for keeping the information gathered from monitoring and the storage settings that enforce it.

T3.2.3.name: Anomaly alerts and evaluation records
T3.2.3.description: Records of alerts on anomalous behavior in networks, systems and applications and of the evaluation of potential information security incidents.

T3.2.3.name: National, Emirate and sector monitoring capability check
T3.2.3.description: Assessment showing the security capabilities across the monitored environment meet national, Emirate or sectoral considerations.

T3.2.4.name: Date and time standard
T3.2.4.description: Definition of the standardized date and time format and the agreed accurate reference time source used across systems.

T3.2.4.name: Time synchronization configuration
T3.2.4.description: Configuration showing systems use the standard format and synchronize with the agreed time source, from a sample of systems.

T3.2.4.name: Clock synchronization check results
T3.2.4.description: Results of regular checks that the clocks of all relevant systems are synchronized.

T3.3.1.name: Threat information sources
T3.3.1.description: List of the external and internal sources selected for threat information, covering strategic, tactical and operational threat intelligence.

T3.3.1.name: Collected threat information
T3.3.1.description: Samples of threat information gathered from the selected sources, such as advisories and indicator feeds.

T3.3.1.name: Threat analysis reports
T3.3.1.description: Analysis of the gathered threat information showing its relevance to the entity.

T3.3.1.name: Actions taken on threat intelligence
T3.3.1.description: Records of the actions taken because of threat intelligence, such as new detection or blocking rules, patching and warnings to teams.

T3.3.2.name: Vulnerability management procedure
T3.3.2.description: Procedure defining the roles and responsibilities for vulnerability monitoring, risk assessment, updating and asset tracking.

T3.3.2.name: Pre-production vulnerability assessment
T3.3.2.description: Vulnerability assessment results and the remediation plan for new systems and applications before they enter production.

T3.3.2.name: Production vulnerability scan results
T3.3.2.description: Results of the tests and scans that check for vulnerabilities in production systems.

T3.3.2.name: Vulnerability remediation tracker
T3.3.2.description: Tracker showing the measure taken for each identified vulnerability, with owner, due date and status.

T3.4.1.name: Approved cryptographic policy
T3.4.1.description: Documented policy, approved and enforced, with the governance that supports the implementation of encryption requirements.

T3.4.1.name: Encryption requirements register
T3.4.1.description: Register of the encryption requirements identified to address security and privacy risks, for data at rest and data in motion.

T3.4.1.name: Cryptographic compliance monitoring
T3.4.1.description: Records of monitoring that the cryptographic practices in use comply with applicable laws, regulations and standards.

T3.4.1.name: Weak cipher and algorithm replacement
T3.4.1.description: Inventory or scan of the ciphers and hashing algorithms in use, with the plan and records for replacing weak or outdated ones.

T3.4.2.name: Encryption at rest settings
T3.4.2.description: Settings showing classified data at rest is encrypted on file servers and storage, with the algorithm and key strength used.

T3.4.2.name: End-user device encryption status
T3.4.2.description: Report from device management showing encryption is enabled on laptops, desktops, smartphones and tablets that hold classified data.

T3.4.2.name: Database and portable media encryption settings
T3.4.2.description: Settings showing databases and portable storage media holding classified data are encrypted.

T3.4.2.name: Encryption in motion configuration
T3.4.2.description: Configuration of the protocols and ciphers protecting data in motion over system interfaces, public networks and electronic messaging.

T3.4.2.name: Transmission encryption test results
T3.4.2.description: Results of scans or tests showing classified data transmissions are encrypted and weak protocols are disabled.

T3.4.3.name: Key management procedure
T3.4.3.description: Procedure covering the cryptographic key life cycle: creation, distribution, storage, recovery, disposal and archival.

T3.4.3.name: Key storage settings
T3.4.3.description: Evidence keys are stored securely, such as hardware security module or key vault settings and the access permissions on them.

T3.4.3.name: Key recovery test records
T3.4.3.description: Records of key recovery tests or incidents showing keys can be recovered after loss or corruption.

T3.4.3.name: Key management activity records
T3.4.3.description: Log extract of key management activities such as creation, access, rotation and disposal.

T3.4.4.name: Public key cryptography inventory
T3.4.4.description: Inventory of the systems and applications that use public key cryptography.

T3.4.4.name: Post-quantum transition plan
T3.4.4.description: Plan for moving systems to quantum-safe cryptography, including the dependency analysis that sets the order of transition.

T3.4.4.name: Post-quantum laboratory test results
T3.4.4.description: Results of testing the new post-quantum cryptographic standard in a laboratory environment before it is used in production.

T3.4.4.name: Post-quantum workforce training records
T3.4.4.description: Records of the awareness and training given to the workforce on the upcoming transition to post-quantum cryptography.

T4.1.1.name: Approved network security policy
T4.1.1.description: Documented policy, approved by management, on the use of network services and devices.

T4.1.1.name: Network diagram
T4.1.1.description: Current network diagram, with version and date, showing all network components, their interconnectivity and their connections to other networks.

T4.1.1.name: Network access control configuration
T4.1.1.description: Configuration showing equipment and devices are detected, restricted and authenticated when they connect to the network, such as port security or network access control settings.

T4.1.1.name: Network risk assessment
T4.1.1.description: Risk assessment of individual network components and of the overall network, identifying the vulnerabilities that need action.

T4.1.1.name: Network control implementation record
T4.1.1.description: Record linking each identified network vulnerability to the specific control implemented to mitigate it.

T4.1.1.name: Traffic control and monitoring configuration
T4.1.1.description: Configuration of the measures that control and monitor incoming and outgoing network traffic, such as firewall rule sets and traffic monitoring settings.

T4.1.2.name: Network services security requirements
T4.1.2.description: List of the network services, in-house or outsourced, that are subject to specific security requirements, with the security features, service levels and management requirements of each.

T4.1.2.name: Network service level agreements
T4.1.2.description: Service level agreements with network service providers that include the minimum security requirements for each service.

T4.1.2.name: Network provider assurance records
T4.1.2.description: Results of checks that providers deliver the agreed services securely, including exercise of the right to audit and any third-party attestations.

T4.1.3.name: Network segregation criteria
T4.1.3.description: Criteria for grouping information services, users and information systems into separate network groups, and the resulting groups or domains.

T4.1.3.name: Network segregation configuration
T4.1.3.description: VLAN, subnet and firewall zone configuration showing the groups are segregated, including the management network.

T4.1.3.name: Segregation requirements in the development life cycle
T4.1.3.description: Extracts from the system and service development life cycle showing the segregation requirements of each group are identified and integrated.

T4.1.3.name: Segregation effectiveness evaluation
T4.1.3.description: Periodic evaluation of how effective the implemented segregation is, such as test results, with the improvements identified.

T4.1.4.name: Wireless site survey
T4.1.4.description: Documented site survey determining the best physical locations for wireless equipment so that stray radio coverage does not reach far outside the entity's physical perimeter.

T4.1.4.name: Wireless segregation configuration
T4.1.4.description: Configuration showing guest internet access is separated from corporate wireless access.

T4.1.4.name: Wireless security controls by network
T4.1.4.description: Record of the security controls required for each wireless network, such as authentication and encryption, based on the protection level of the services, users and systems it supports.

T4.1.4.name: Wireless usage and configuration standard
T4.1.4.description: Document stating the usage restrictions, configuration requirements and implementation guidance for wireless access.

T4.1.5.name: Website access categories
T4.1.5.description: Definition of the types of websites personnel should and should not be able to reach, for example sites with upload functions, known malicious sites and command and control servers.

T4.1.5.name: Web filter configuration
T4.1.5.description: Web filtering configuration showing the blocked categories and the blocking of websites with illegal information, viruses or phishing material.

T4.1.5.name: Web filter block records
T4.1.5.description: Log extract of requests blocked because the site holds illegal information, viruses or phishing material.

T5.1.1.name: Approved identity and access management policy
T5.1.1.description: Documented policy, approved by management and based on business and security requirements, covering identity management, user access management, access rights review, privileged access management, secure authentication and password management.

T5.1.1.name: Access requirements set by owners
T5.1.1.description: Record of the business and security requirements for access that information and asset owners have determined, which the policy takes account of.

T5.1.1.name: Access policy communication
T5.1.1.description: Evidence the policy was communicated to all relevant interested parties.

T5.2.1.name: User identity list
T5.2.1.description: Export of user accounts showing a unique identifier for each user, a separate account for each individual and no shared accounts.

T5.2.1.name: Identity life cycle procedure
T5.2.1.description: Procedure for creating, changing, disabling and removing identities, including the approval and documentation required for any shared or non-human identity.

T5.2.1.name: Disabled and removed identity records
T5.2.1.description: Records showing identities were disabled or removed promptly when no longer needed, checked against leaver records.

T5.2.1.name: Restricted identity activity records
T5.2.1.description: Log extract of the activities performed by restricted identities.

T5.2.2.name: Access provisioning and de-provisioning procedure
T5.2.2.description: Formal procedure for granting, changing and removing access rights, including owner authorization and activation of rights only after authorization is complete.

T5.2.2.name: Segregation of duties matrix
T5.2.2.description: Matrix of conflicting roles showing that approval and implementation of access rights are separated.

T5.2.2.name: Access rights records
T5.2.2.description: Records of the access rights granted for all assets, identifying any special access.

T5.2.2.name: Role change and leaver revocation records
T5.2.2.description: Records, checked against joiner, mover and leaver data, showing access was revoked immediately when users changed role or left the entity.

T5.2.2.name: Temporary and inactive account review
T5.2.2.description: Periodic check of temporary and inactive accounts, with the access revoked as a result.

T5.2.3.name: Privileged access register
T5.2.3.description: Record of all allocated privileges by system and account, with the formal authorization for each.

T5.2.3.name: Administrative group membership export
T5.2.3.description: Export of domain and local administrator group members showing regular users hold no administrative privileges.

T5.2.3.name: Administrator account usage rules
T5.2.3.description: Evidence administrator accounts are used only for system administration, such as separate administrator accounts and the restriction of email and web browsing on them.

T5.2.3.name: Administrative multi-factor authentication settings
T5.2.3.description: Configuration showing multi-factor authentication is required for all administrative access.

T5.2.3.name: Local administrator password controls
T5.2.3.description: Settings showing a different password is used on each local administrator account, such as a local password management tool.

T5.2.3.name: Administrative activity logs and reviews
T5.2.3.description: Logs of all administrative access activity with records of the regular reviews and of the response to suspicious or unauthorized activity.

T5.2.4.name: Access rights review procedure
T5.2.4.description: Procedure for reviewing access rights periodically and after any change in user status, such as promotion, demotion or termination.

T5.2.4.name: Completed access rights reviews
T5.2.4.description: Completed review records with the reviewer's sign-off and the access removed or changed as a result.

T5.2.4.name: Special access validity checks
T5.2.4.description: Checks of granted special and privileged access, at shorter intervals than general reviews, showing each grant is still valid.

T5.3.1.name: Information system authentication configuration
T5.3.1.description: Authentication settings showing strong techniques are used on information systems, with strength matched to the classification of the information accessed.

T5.3.1.name: Secure log-on and log-off settings
T5.3.1.description: Evidence of the secure log-on and log-off procedure, such as settings that limit failed attempts and end sessions at log-off.

T5.3.1.name: Maximum session time settings
T5.3.1.description: Settings for the maximum session time of authenticated users on sensitive systems and applications.

T5.3.1.name: Inactivity timeout settings
T5.3.1.description: Settings showing inactive sessions are terminated after the predefined period of inactivity.

T5.3.2.name: Access restriction model
T5.3.2.description: Description of how access to information and associated assets is restricted by role, including that classified information is not available to anonymous or unknown identities.

T5.3.2.name: Role-based access matrix
T5.3.2.description: Matrix mapping roles and responsibilities to the access rights granted to information and associated assets.

T5.3.2.name: System access control settings
T5.3.2.description: Access control settings from sampled systems, applications and services showing who can access what information and at what level.

T5.3.2.name: Business-need access adjustments
T5.3.2.description: Records of access changes made for individual users and support personnel because of specific business needs, with the approval given.

T5.3.3.name: Secure remote access configuration
T5.3.3.description: Configuration showing all remote connections by users and administrators go through secure channels, such as VPN settings.

T5.3.3.name: Remote authentication method settings
T5.3.3.description: Settings showing the authentication methods required of remote users, such as certificates, hardware tokens or multi-factor authentication.

T5.3.3.name: Remote administrator access approvals
T5.3.3.description: Approvals given before remote administrator-level access was granted.

T5.3.3.name: Remote administrator access monitoring
T5.3.3.description: Log extract showing remote administrator-level sessions are controlled and monitored.

T5.3.4.name: Utility program authorization list
T5.3.4.description: List of the utility programs able to override system and application controls and the authorized personnel allowed to use them, with the authorization levels.

T5.3.4.name: Utility access restriction settings
T5.3.4.description: Settings showing utility programs can be used only by authorized personnel and unnecessary utilities are removed or disabled.

T5.3.4.name: Utility program usage records
T5.3.4.description: Log extract of the use of utility programs.

T5.4.1.name: Credential issuance procedure
T5.4.1.description: Procedure for providing security credentials securely, including identity verification before issue, temporary credentials changed at first use, secure delivery, revocation and re-allocation.

T5.4.1.name: Credential issuance records
T5.4.1.description: Sample records of credentials issued, re-allocated or revoked, with the date and the person who authorized each.

T5.4.1.name: Initial credential generation and delivery settings
T5.4.1.description: Evidence initial credentials are generated as non-guessable, unique values and delivered over a protected channel rather than in clear text email.

T5.4.2.name: Credential use good practices
T5.4.2.description: Guidance on good use of security credentials, such as keeping them confidential, not recording them insecurely, changing them after possible compromise and choosing quality passwords.

T5.4.2.name: Good practice communication records
T5.4.2.description: Evidence the good practices were communicated to users, such as notices, induction material or awareness sessions.

T5.4.2.name: Approved credential storage method
T5.4.2.description: Record of the approved ways for users to store credentials securely, such as a password vault.

T5.4.3.name: Credential change automation
T5.4.3.description: Evidence the credential change procedure is automated and verifies the user's identity before a change, such as self-service reset settings.

T5.4.3.name: Credential strength settings
T5.4.3.description: Settings that validate the strength of changed credentials, such as minimum length and complexity, and that lock accounts after a set number of failed attempts.

T5.4.3.name: Credential lifetime and reuse settings
T5.4.3.description: Settings for the maximum lifetime of credentials and the conditions on reuse, including the history of previous credentials.

T5.4.3.name: First access password change enforcement
T5.4.3.description: Evidence default and temporary passwords must be changed at first access.

T5.4.3.name: Credential storage protection
T5.4.3.description: Evidence credentials are stored hashed with salt or encrypted, such as the hashing settings of the credential store.

T6.1.1.name: Approved third-party security policy
T6.1.1.description: Documented policy, approved by management, that provides the framework for third-party risk management.

T6.1.1.name: Third-party security governance arrangements
T6.1.1.description: Governance for third-party security: responsibilities, oversight forum, resources (budget, people and tools) and the communication channels between suppliers, internal departments and partners.

T6.1.1.name: Third-party security program mandate
T6.1.1.description: Senior leadership's mandate establishing the third-party security program, with the resources assigned to it.

T6.2.1.name: Third-party risk management procedure
T6.2.1.description: Approved procedure for managing the information security risks of third-party products and services, including cloud services, covering the start and the end of the relationship.

T6.2.1.name: Supplier risk classification register
T6.2.1.description: Register of third-party suppliers classified by the risk they pose to the entity's systems and data.

T6.2.1.name: Third-party cyber security risk assessments
T6.2.1.description: Assessments of the cyber security risks of sampled suppliers and of their products or services across the supply chain.

T6.2.1.name: Supplier risk mitigation plans
T6.2.1.description: Strategies and actions to mitigate the identified supplier risks, with owner and status, and the continuous monitoring they put in place.

T6.2.2.name: Supplier security assessment criteria
T6.2.2.description: Assessment template and criteria for judging a supplier's information security posture, covering topics such as governance, secure design and code, physical security, monitoring and auditing, and incident response and recovery.

T6.2.2.name: Completed supplier security assessments
T6.2.2.description: Assessments of sampled suppliers completed against the criteria during selection, with the results and the decision reached.

T6.2.2.name: Supplier due diligence records
T6.2.2.description: Records of the due diligence checks that verify a supplier's cyber security posture before onboarding and again at intervals set by its criticality.

T6.2.3.name: ICT supply chain security procedure
T6.2.3.description: Approved procedure for managing the information security risks of the ICT products and services supply chain.

T6.2.3.name: Procurement security requirements
T6.2.3.description: Defined security requirements for hardware and software procurement, such as authentication and authorization mechanisms, data encryption and security protocols.

T6.2.3.name: Pre-procurement product evaluations
T6.2.3.description: Evaluations of sampled hardware and software products against the security requirements before they were bought.

T6.2.3.name: System acceptance test results
T6.2.3.description: Test results and sign-off showing tests were completed before new systems were accepted into the operational environment.

T6.2.3.name: Supply chain upgrade and maintenance records
T6.2.3.description: Records showing hardware and software supplied through the ICT supply chain is upgraded and maintained in a timely and secure way.

T6.2.4.name: Supplier contract security clause templates
T6.2.4.description: Standard information security clauses used in supplier contracts, adjusted to the type of relationship with the supplier.

T6.2.4.name: Executed supplier contracts
T6.2.4.description: Sample signed supplier contracts showing the information security requirements are embedded, including that suppliers pass them on to sub-contractors and step-in rights where relevant.

T6.2.4.name: Legal and regulatory compliance clauses
T6.2.4.description: Contract clauses obliging suppliers to comply with the applicable laws and regulations.

T6.2.5.name: Supplier monitoring program
T6.2.5.description: Program describing how supplier adherence to the contractual cyber security requirements is monitored, including logging and auditing of supplier access to the entity's information and critical systems.

T6.2.5.name: Supplier access monitoring records
T6.2.5.description: Log extract of supplier activity on the entity's information and critical systems, retained for investigation and accountability.

T6.2.5.name: Supplier assessments and audit reports
T6.2.5.description: Assessments, audits or evaluations verifying suppliers comply with the specified security controls and measures.

T6.2.5.name: Supplier change management records
T6.2.5.description: Records of changes in supplier security practices and service delivery, with the entity's assessment and handling of each change.

T7.1.1.name: Approved acquisition, development and maintenance policy
T7.1.1.description: Documented policy, approved by management, that fits the relationship between the entity and the internal and external parties involved and outlines their roles and responsibilities.

T7.1.1.name: Policy framework for security in the life cycle
T7.1.1.description: Framework in the policy for integrating information security controls through acquiring, designing, developing, implementing and maintaining systems, in-house or outsourced, including environment separation, secure coding, security in design and testing checkpoints.

T7.1.1.name: Policy communication to internal and external parties
T7.1.1.description: Evidence the policy was shared with the internal and external parties involved, with the sign-off that approved it.

T7.2.1.name: Application security requirements specification
T7.2.1.description: Information security requirements identified, specified and approved for sampled applications developed or acquired, drawn from a risk assessment.

T7.2.1.name: Requirements by application purpose
T7.2.1.description: Requirements set for the purpose of each application, including controls for transactional services, electronic commerce and payment applications where applicable.

T7.2.1.name: Application requirements implementation evidence
T7.2.1.description: Test results or design reviews showing the application security requirements were implemented in sampled applications.

T7.2.2.name: Secure engineering principles
T7.2.2.description: Approved document establishing the principles for engineering secure systems, such as user authentication techniques, secure session control and data validation and sanitization.

T7.2.2.name: Principles applied across architecture layers
T7.2.2.description: Architecture documents showing the principles are applied consistently across the business, data, application and infrastructure layers.

T7.2.2.name: Security design reviews
T7.2.2.description: Reviews of sampled designs against known attack patterns and the security risks of new components.

T7.3.1.name: Secure coding guidelines
T7.3.1.description: Documented and approved secure coding practices, with the minimum secure baseline, extended to third-party and open-source components.

T7.3.1.name: Secure coding use evidence
T7.3.1.description: Evidence the practices are used during development, such as code review records and completed checklists.

T7.3.1.name: Automated security testing results
T7.3.1.description: Results of the automated security tests run during and after deployment, with the findings and how they were fixed.

T7.3.1.name: Developer security training records
T7.3.1.description: Records of the application security knowledge and training given to developers.

T7.3.2.name: Quality assurance process
T7.3.2.description: Defined quality assurance process for outsourced development, including acceptance testing of the quality and accuracy of deliverables.

T7.3.2.name: Secure coding and QA contract clauses
T7.3.2.description: Clauses in the software acquisition contract obliging the third party to follow the entity's secure coding policy and quality assurance process.

T7.3.2.name: Contractual security requirements
T7.3.2.description: Requirements and information security functionality specified in the software development contract, together with code ownership and licensing terms.

T7.3.2.name: Delivered code checks
T7.3.2.description: Results of checks of delivered code for vulnerabilities, malicious code or code that does not conform to the required functionality.

T7.3.2.name: Outsourced development review records
T7.3.2.description: Records showing the entity directs, monitors and reviews the outsourced work against the agreed expectations.

T7.3.3.name: Source code access permissions
T7.3.3.description: Read and write permissions on source code repositories, development tools and software libraries, aligned with the access control policy.

T7.3.3.name: Source code permission reviews
T7.3.3.description: Records of the periodic reviews of the permissions and the changes made as a result.

T7.3.3.name: Source code access audit log
T7.3.3.description: Audit log extract of all accesses to source code, development tools and software libraries.

T7.4.1.name: Change control procedure for systems and software
T7.4.1.description: Documented change control procedure for information processing facilities and information systems, integrated for infrastructure and software where practicable.

T7.4.1.name: Change track record
T7.4.1.description: Track record of all changes showing the request, approval, implementation and outcome of each.

T7.4.1.name: Software version archive
T7.4.1.description: Evidence a copy of every software version is kept, with the integrity verification applied, such as hash checks.

T7.4.1.name: Change rollback procedures
T7.4.1.description: Rollback procedures defined for sampled changes.

T7.4.1.name: Pre-production change test results
T7.4.1.description: Results of testing sampled changes in a test environment before they were moved to production.

T7.4.1.name: Change implementation planning
T7.4.1.description: Plans for sampled changes showing the implementation was scheduled for the right time and the stakeholders were told.

T7.4.2.name: Test data selection rules
T7.4.2.description: Rules for selecting test data, using sample data sets and keeping classified and personal information out of development and test environments.

T7.4.2.name: Production data copy authorizations
T7.4.2.description: Authorization for each transfer of real data from the production environment to a test environment.

T7.4.2.name: Test environment access settings
T7.4.2.description: Access control settings showing test environments that hold copies of operational data are protected as the operational environment is.

T7.4.2.name: Test data erasure records
T7.4.2.description: Records that data was erased from test applications immediately after testing was completed.

T7.4.2.name: Test data movement log
T7.4.2.description: Log of every copy and erasure of data between the production and test environments.

T7.4.3.name: Security testing requirements
T7.4.3.description: Defined requirements for testing the security of new and updated systems before they go live, such as security functions, secure coding and secure configurations.

T7.4.3.name: Acceptance parameters for security tests
T7.4.3.description: Acceptable parameters for each testing requirement, such as pass thresholds.

T7.4.3.name: Security test results
T7.4.3.description: Documented results of the security tests carried out on sampled new or updated systems.

T7.4.3.name: Test completion responsibility assignment
T7.4.3.description: Formal assignment of responsibility for ensuring security tests are completed before systems are accepted, with the sign-off on sampled acceptances.

T8.1.1.name: Approved incident management policy
T8.1.1.description: Documented policy, approved by management, that outlines the roles and responsibilities for incident management and provides the framework for managing incidents, including classification and handling requirements.

T8.1.1.name: Incident handling and reporting requirements
T8.1.1.description: Register of the Emirate, sector and national requirements for handling and reporting incidents, with the policy provision that addresses each.

T8.1.1.name: Incident management policy approval record
T8.1.1.description: Sign-off showing the policy was approved and which version is in force.

T8.1.2.name: Event reporting procedure
T8.1.2.description: Procedure and mechanism for reporting observed or suspected information security events, with the point of contact, designed to be easy to use and always available.

T8.1.2.name: Event reporting awareness records
T8.1.2.description: Evidence employees, contractors and third parties were made aware of their responsibility to report events as quickly as possible, such as awareness material and induction content.

T8.1.2.name: Reporting channel evidence
T8.1.2.description: Screenshot or published contact details of the reporting channel, such as a hotline, mailbox or portal, showing the point of contact is accessible.

T8.1.2.name: Reported event records
T8.1.2.description: Sample of events reported through the mechanism, showing it is used and the events reach the point of contact.

T8.2.1.name: Incident response plan
T8.2.1.description: Plan describing the structure of the incident response capability and the processes and procedures for handling incidents before, during and after an incident.

T8.2.1.name: Incident communication plan
T8.2.1.description: Plan for communicating with internal and external parties during an incident.

T8.2.1.name: Senior management approval of response plans
T8.2.1.description: Sign-off by senior management of the incident response plan and all related plans and procedures.

T8.2.1.name: Incident response resources and capabilities
T8.2.1.description: Definition of the resources and capabilities required for incident response and the management support needed to maintain them.

T8.2.1.name: Incident Response Team establishment
T8.2.1.description: Charter or appointment records establishing the Incident Response Team, with its members, roles and contact details.

T8.2.2.name: Incident classification and prioritization scheme
T8.2.2.description: Documented scheme for classifying and prioritizing incidents by impact, in line with the incident management policy and the CSC issuances on incident management.

T8.2.2.name: National agency reporting criteria
T8.2.2.description: Criteria identifying the incidents that must be reported to national agencies under Emirate, sector and national requirements, with the notification times by incident level.

T8.2.2.name: Classified incident records
T8.2.2.description: Sample incident records showing the classification and priority assigned and the decision on whether to report to national agencies.

T8.2.3.name: Incident response training needs analysis
